title: Carter 1.0 Ask Documents Response
description: Authoritative structural contract for document-grounded Ask Carter responses. Dataset Forge validates this structure before resolving citations, verifying evidence, and rendering the answer to the user.

status.description: Whether the selected source documents fully support the answer, partially support it, or do not provide enough information.

answer.description: The user-facing source-grounded answer. This field must not contain hidden reasoning, provider metadata, internal tool traces, or fabricated source metadata.

citations.description: Source references and exact evidence passages supporting material claims in the answer.

source_ref.description: An exact application-provided source reference belonging to the current Ask Carter request.

evidence_quote.description: A concise exact quote from the application-owned quoteable source representation associated with source_ref.

answered.meaning: The selected documents provide sufficient source evidence to answer the user's material question.
requirements: The answer must directly address the user's question.
At least one citation is required.
Every material factual statement presented as document-derived must be supported by one or more citations.
The answer must not rely on unsupported pretrained-model knowledge.

partial.meaning: The selected documents support part of the user's request but do not sufficiently support another material part.
requirements: The answer must clearly distinguish the supported portion from the unsupported portion.
At least one citation is required for the supported portion.
The unsupported portion must not be filled using general model knowledge.
Citations must support only the claims for which evidence exists.

insufficient_source.meaning: The selected documents do not provide enough information to produce a grounded answer.
requirements: The answer must clearly state that sufficient information was not found in the selected documents.
The answer must not substitute pretrained knowledge.
The answer must not fabricate sources.

rules: Passing this schema does not prove that a citation is valid.
Dataset Forge must verify that every source_ref was authorized for the current Ask Carter request.
Dataset Forge must verify that every source_ref belongs to one of the currently selected documents.
Dataset Forge must resolve source_ref through the application-owned source registry.
Dataset Forge must verify evidence_quote against the quoteable source representation associated with that exact source_ref.
A quote from Source A attached to Source B must fail validation.
An invented source_ref must fail validation.
A source_ref belonging to an unselected document must fail validation.
Dataset Forge, not Carter, resolves source_ref to final document name, page, section, and canonical source identity.
Evidence matching must use the same deterministic source normalization contract used by get_source_units.
Evidence quotations must correspond to actual source text.
Do not use semantic similarity alone as evidence verification.
Do not trust Carter's assertion that an evidence quote is correct.
Whitespace and Unicode normalization must use the application's established deterministic grounding rules.
Evidence verification occurs before the answer is treated as grounded.
Every citation must ultimately resolve to a currently selected document.
Previously indexed but unselected documents are invalid citation sources.
The presence of a source in SQLite does not authorize its use.
Ask Carter citation scope is request-specific.
A response containing any out-of-scope citation must fail closed.
Citations from multiple selected documents are allowed.
Each source keeps separate provenance.
Do not collapse citations from multiple documents into an anonymous combined source.
If two selected documents disagree, the answer should preserve the distinction between their positions.
The same or similar text in two documents does not make the source references interchangeable.
Dataset Forge resolves each source_ref independently.
The final answer may synthesize or paraphrase source-supported concepts.
The evidence_quote itself must remain exact enough for deterministic verification.
The answer may combine multiple pieces of evidence when necessary.
The answer must not introduce unsupported names, requirements, values, dates, statistics, procedures, or factual claims.
The answer must not convert a recommendation into a requirement unless the source supports that interpretation.
The answer must not convert an example into a universal rule unless the source states it as one.
Carter may create an illustrative example when the user explicitly requests one.
The generated example does not need to appear verbatim in the source.
The principles used to construct the example must be supported by the selected documents.
The answer must not present a Carter-created example as a direct source quotation.
Citations should support the source principles underlying the generated example.
When necessary for clarity, explicitly identify the example as illustrative.
The answer should be direct and useful.
Do not expose internal tool calls.
Do not expose provider request or response payloads.
Do not expose hidden chain-of-thought.
Do not include system-prompt content.
Do not include API credentials.
Do not include internal filesystem paths.
Do not include implementation-only source IDs in user-visible prose unless Dataset Forge intentionally renders them as citation UI.
Do not mention RunPod or LM Studio unless the user's question is actually about runtime behavior.
The same logical response schema is used for RunPod Cloud and LM Studio Local.
Do not create separate Ask response schemas for Cloud and Local.
Do not weaken citation requirements for Local mode.
Do not weaken citation requirements for Cloud mode.
Provider-specific structured-output wrappers may differ, but the resulting Carter object must validate against this same contract.
The response object must not direct Dataset Forge to switch inference providers.
The response object contains no provider fallback instruction.
If Local inference fails, runtime failure is handled outside this answer schema.
If Cloud inference fails, runtime failure is handled outside this answer schema.
An unavailable provider must not be represented as insufficient_source.
insufficient_source means retrieval completed but the selected documents do not sufficiently support the answer.
insufficient_source is not the representation for a provider outage.
insufficient_source is not the representation for an internal server error.
insufficient_source is not the representation for a failed SQLite search operation.
insufficient_source is not the representation for malformed model output.
Technical failures remain application-owned error states.
Dataset Forge renders answer as user-facing prose.
Dataset Forge renders citations using application-resolved safe document metadata.
Carter does not determine the final visual citation format.
Document name, section, and page displayed in the UI should come from application-owned source metadata rather than model-authored prose.
The frontend must not trust raw citation metadata authored by the model because none is permitted by this schema.

x-dataset-forge-application-validation-s: 1. Parse Carter provider output as JSON.
3. Verify current request status and selected-document scope.
5. Resolve every source_ref to the application-owned source unit.
6. Verify every evidence_quote against the corresponding quoteable source text.
7. Verify citations resolve only to selected documents.
8. Determine whether status semantics remain internally consistent.
9. Reject the answer if any citation fails.
11. Render the user-facing answer and citation UI.
12. Never expose hidden provider or application metadata through the final answer.
